key_insight: ImageNet pretraining improved vocal fold boundary segmentation, bringing Swin-UNet to performance similar to pretrained TransUNet with roughly one-quarter of its trainable parameters.
engineering_relevance: Automated vocal fold segmentation could reduce manual processing in intraglottal PIV and support measurements of tissue dynamics and airflow under challenging optical conditions.
method: Benchmarked UNet, UNet++, TransUNet, and Swin-UNet across six pipelines.
Compared transformer-based models trained from scratch versus ImageNet-pretrained weights.
Evaluated overlap and boundary fidelity using DSC, BF1, and HD95.
evidence_signal: Using 16,344 expert-annotated images from 227 ex vivo canine phonation trials, pipelines were trained with five seeds and compared on 50 held-out trials using Holm-corrected, trial-level Wilcoxon tests; mean DSC ranged from 0.9734 to 0.9764.
watch_item: Validation was limited to ex vivo canine images; generalization to other imaging setups or in vivo conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in Ex Vivo High-Speed Phonation Images
